structured.approach: I read the two contracted inputs. feat.tasks gives the Data Science lane's tasks and its repository. org.engineering_stack gives the language, CI command, branch rules and whether Databricks is used. Shell commands are blocked in DS-01 by the G9 hook, so availability, the branch's origin and write access come from the spine's repo-access tool view. I checked that view against the git files in the checkout: HEAD, refs/heads/main, refs/heads/dev, the feature/story reflog and .git/config. To describe the starting point for TSK-03 and TSK-04, I read ci.py, src/ap_forecast/__init__.py, predict.py, explain.py and tests/test_forecast.py in full, and the repository's CLAUDE.md. Every file cited in the output was read in this session. I then wrote task.repo_access in full. I used no connector, because the inputs and the checkout held every fact needed.

claims.text: The Data Science lane owns TSK-03 (STORY-03, vendor_risk) and TSK-04 (STORY-04, build_explanation_request risk parameter), both in repository ap_forecast.
ap_forecast is Python 3.9 with unittest and CI command /usr/bin/python3 ci.py; every CI enforces line coverage >= 90%.
No repository uses Databricks or a database, and ap_forecast uses no Databricks or other workspace.
ap_forecast is available locally and the agent identity has write access; git status is clean, so no repository creation is needed.
The working branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, and HEAD points to refs/heads/feature/story.
main and dev both point to d67e8662907401467a3f76f9f167e7a60d89ffca, and the feature/story reflog shows it was created at that same commit.
Remote origin is configured on GitHub and main and dev track it; feature/story has no upstream configured.
predict.py defines predict_delay_days(history) and explain.py defines load_config() and build_explanation_request(vendor, predicted_days, config=None).

tests/test_forecast.py has the ForecastTest class with test_predict, test_request_uses_config and test_request_with_explicit_config; TSK-03 adds tests/test_risk.py and TSK-04 extends tests/test_forecast.py.
Current package version is 0.9.0 and __all__ exports predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request.
ci.py sets COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0, flags print/eval/exec, bare except and lines longer than 140 characters, and imports the third-party coverage package.
Branch convention is main (released), dev (integration), feature/<story>; commit messages start with the story ID.

open_questions: RAQ-1: Is the third-party coverage package that ci.py imports installed for /usr/bin/python3 on the runner? Interim answer: assume yes; the first CI run in the coding steps will confirm it.

RAQ-2: Should STORY-03 and STORY-04 each get its own branch (feature/STORY-03 and feature/STORY-04) instead of sharing the single feature/story? Interim answer: use feature/story for both, with commit messages that start with the story ID.
structured.summary: The coding prerequisites are in place, and task.repo_access is rewritten in full. The Data Science lane only needs ap_forecast, for TSK-03 and TSK-04. It is checked out locally, the agent identity has write access and the working tree is clean. Work happens on feature/story, which was created from dev at d67e866 and has no commits yet. No repository needs to be created, and no Databricks or database access is needed. Shell commands are blocked in this step, so I ran no git or CI command. Availability and write access come from the spine's repo-access tool view, which I checked against the git files in the checkout. I read tests/test_forecast.py in full, so the claims about existing tests now cite a file read in this session. Two questions remain, neither blocking. First, the coverage package that CI needs has not been confirmed as installed. Second, STORY-03 and STORY-04 share the single feature/story branch, while the convention is one branch per story.
